To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce a novel preconditioner for the PCG method applied to symmetric Toeplitz matrices and prove its effectiveness in the case of a continuous generating function with isolated zeros of even multiplicity.

(a) for strictly positive generating functions, the optimal τ matrix is not the best choice for preconditioning, and that (b) in the ill-conditioning case, the natural τ matrix can be a bad choice, and that the proposed τ matrix, defined in the paper, is a better one.

the natural and optimal τ matrices can be used as preconditioners for the solution of symmetric Toeplitz linear systems with nonnegative generating functions, and that a suitable preconditioner for the solution of systems with generating functions having isolated zeros is a new τ matrix which requires the solution of a small number of auxiliary problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the solution of large-scale Toeplitz linear systems with nonnegative generating functions by means of PCG methods, and with the design of a suitable preconditioner for the given system.
the solution of Toeplitz systems by means of PCG methods and the related theoretical and numerical results can be considered a contribution to this field.
the development of new PCG methods for Toeplitz matrices with a superlinear rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for symmetric Toeplitt systems, the PCG method with the optimal preconditioner proposed by Bini–Di Benedetto is a good method for the well-conditioned case, while, for the ill-conditioned one, the PCG with the new τ matrix is a good method.

, for the solution of a given symmetric Toeplitz system, the optimal τ matrix is a good preconditioner only if the generating function f is strictly positive, or if the ill-conditioning of the system is moderate.
the proposed PCG method is a very effective tool for solving symmetric Toeplitz linear systems with nonnegative generating functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to solve a symmetric Toeplitz system in O(n log n + s) ops, where s is the number of isolated zeros of even degree.

we are able to solve symmetric Toeplitz linear systems by means of PCG methods with a total arithmetic cost O(n log n), and a superlinear rate in the case of nonnegative generating function, and a sublinear rate in the ill-conditioning case.
, by means of our PCG method, we can solve Toeplitz linear systems in a time which is almost the same as the one needed to solve a single Toeplitz system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of Toeplitz matrices, the choice of the preconditioner is not so important as it is in the case of general matrices.
, in order to solve symmetric Toeplitz linear systems, it is important to use a preconditioner which is not necessarily optimal, but which is positive definite.

, in the case of Toeplitz systems with isolated singularities, the use of a suitable preconditioner can lead to a superlinear convergence rate of the PCG method, and this is not possible if the preconditioner is chosen in an inappropriate way.
